correctness.rationale: Principal ideal descent along finite cycles for \(\theta\) and \(\delta\) yields \((\alpha(x))=(x)=(x^2)\). Nilpotents vanish, so \(R\) is a product of finite fields. Singleton support strata give a multiplicative \(-1=1\) contradiction in odd fields and an additive zero-collision for each \(\mathbb F_2\) factor. Conversely coordinatewise \(a\ne0,1\) makes \(\alpha\), \(x+\alpha(x)\), and \(x\alpha(x)\) all bijections via Frobenius. Script exhaustively checks 14 explicit small ring cases and positive product examples; computations do not substitute for universal proof.

value.rationale: Theorem gives a complete, explicit structural existence classification for a natural subfamily of the simultaneous-operation problem explicitly posed in arXiv:2608.25092v1 Problem 15.12. It separates nilpotent, odd-field and F2 obstructions and covers arbitrary finite direct products with explicit witnesses, beyond a single small-case exercise. The ring \(\mathbb F_2\times\mathbb F_4\) admits additive and multiplicative complete mappings separately but forbids a common one, illustrating genuine interaction between operations.
